Container.Name: Ultrafeeder
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: adsb ads-b readsb tar1090 graphs1090 dump1090 rtl-sdr rtlsdr sdr flightradar24 fr24 flightaware piaware adsbexchange adsb.fi airplanes.live mlat aircraft plane tracker radar bias-tee lna 1090
Container.Overview:
Ultrafeeder is the SDR-Enthusiasts all-in-one ADS-B container: it decodes 1090 MHz aircraft signals from an RTL-SDR dongle with readsb, shows them on a live tar1090 map, graphs your reception with graphs1090, and can feed many aggregators (adsb.fi, airplanes.live, ADSBExchange and others) with MLAT.
It also works as a "receiver" for other feeder containers. For example, the FR24/FlightAware all-in-one containers can take their data from Ultrafeeder's Beast output (port 30005) instead of opening the dongle themselves.
:: QUICK START :: 1. Plug in your RTL-SDR dongle. Make sure no other container (dump1090, fr24feed-piaware, etc.) is using it. 2. Set your receiver latitude, longitude and altitude (metres, e.g. 18m). 3. Start the container and open the WebUI. Aircraft should appear within a minute.
:: POWERING AN LNA (BIAS-TEE) :: If you use a bias-tee powered LNA/filter with an RTL-SDR Blog V3/V4, set "Enable Bias-Tee" to true AND put --enable-biastee in "Extra readsb Arguments". The second setting makes readsb keep the bias-tee on after it opens the dongle; some decoders reset it, which leaves the LNA unpowered and blocking signal.
:: GAIN :: "auto" uses readsb's built-in auto-gain (recommended by SDR-Enthusiasts). You can also set a fixed value in dB, e.g. 40.2.
:: FEEDING AGGREGATORS :: Use ULTRAFEEDER_CONFIG to add feeds, e.g. adsb,feed.adsb.fi,30004,beast_reduce_plus_out;mlat,feed.adsb.fi,31090 and set UUID (generate one with: cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid). See the project README for the full list.
This is a community template. It is not affiliated with SDR-Enthusiasts. Please report template problems via the Support link.
Container.Requires: An RTL-SDR (or other readsb-supported) receiver connected to the Unraid server. Only one container can use a given dongle at a time.

Config.Name: WebUI (tar1090 map)
Config.Description: tar1090 live map, graphs1090 (/graphs1090/) and stats. Change the host port if 8080 is already in use.

Config.Name: Beast output
Config.Description: Beast data output. Point other feeder containers here (host IP:30005), e.g. fr24feed-piaware with SERVICE_ENABLE_IMPORT_OVER_NETCAT.

Config.Name: SBS/BaseStation output
Config.Description: SBS (BaseStation) format output for tools such as Virtual Radar Server.

Config.Name: JSON position output
Config.Description: JSON position output.

Config.Name: Receiver latitude
Config.Description: Your receiver's latitude in decimal degrees, e.g. -28.0875

Config.Name: Receiver longitude
Config.Description: Your receiver's longitude in decimal degrees, e.g. 153.3922

Config.Name: Receiver altitude
Config.Description: Antenna altitude above sea level with unit, e.g. 18m or 60ft

Config.Name: Device type
Config.Description: rtlsdr for RTL-SDR dongles. Other options: modesbeast, gnshulc. Leave empty if this container only receives network data.

Config.Name: RTL-SDR serial
Config.Description: Optional. Serial number of the dongle to use. Only needed if you have more than one RTL-SDR.

Config.Name: Gain
Config.Description: auto = readsb built-in auto-gain (recommended). Or a fixed value in dB such as 40.2. autogain = legacy slow auto-gain script.

Config.Name: PPM correction
Config.Description: Optional oscillator correction in PPM. Usually not needed for TCXO dongles such as the RTL-SDR Blog V3/V4.

Config.Name: Enable Bias-Tee
Config.Description: true to power a bias-tee LNA/filter through the coax (RTL-SDR Blog V3/V4 and similar). Also add --enable-biastee to Extra readsb Arguments.

Config.Name: Extra readsb Arguments
Config.Description: Extra arguments passed to readsb. For a bias-tee powered LNA use: --enable-biastee

Config.Name: Ultrafeeder config (feeds)
Config.Description: Optional semicolon-separated list of feeds/MLAT/inputs. See the project README (ULTRAFEEDER_CONFIG section).

Config.Name: Feeder UUID
Config.Description: Optional. Unique ID sent to aggregators. Generate with: cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid

Config.Name: MLAT user name
Config.Description: Optional. Name shown on aggregator MLAT sync maps.

Config.Name: Location accuracy
Config.Description: 0 = no location, 1 = 2 decimals, 2 = exact, 3 = 1 decimal, 4 = 0 decimals

Config.Name: Collect range statistics
Config.Description: true to collect range statistics for the graphs1090 polar plot.

Config.Name: Update tar1090 at start
Config.Description: true to update tar1090 and its aircraft database at container start.

Config.Name: Map page title
Config.Description: Title shown on the tar1090 map page.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: verbose, error or none

Config.Name: Globe history
Config.Description: Persistent tar1090 history and readsb state.

Config.Name: Graphs data
Config.Description: Persistent graphs1090 data.

Config.Name: USB bus
Config.Description: Gives the container access to the RTL-SDR USB device.

Config.Name: Disk stats (graphs)
Config.Description: Read-only, used by graphs1090 for system graphs.
